description: The signed ConfigResponse the device fetches from the control plane (kseal.v1.ConfigService/GetConfig). It carries the policy (as a signed, cacheable SignedConfig) and, when one is active for the scope, the SignedKillSwitch. Both are Ed25519-signed so the device verifies them OFFLINE against a pinned signing key - a CDN or cache cannot tamper with policy or forge a disable.

config.signature: <Ed25519 over the signed-config preimage; illustrative here - the byte-exact reproducible crypto vectors are control/kill-switch-command.json and reference/golden-vectors.json>

notes: The signed-config signature authenticates the WHOLE envelope (version is the rollback anchor, ttl_seconds the staleness anchor, plus key_id and config_bytes), closing the CDN/cache tamper vector. The Go server and the Rust device core mirror this preimage byte-for-byte, pinned by a shared golden vector. The embedded kill_switch signature above is the REAL, verifiable Ed25519 signature from control/kill-switch-command.json; an absent or invalid kill switch never disables (fail-safe).
